references.text: Jesus said earlier in his conversation with Nicodemus that he testifies to what he has seen, but that no one accepts his testimony ([ref:Joh 3:11|John 3:11]). Verse 32 repeats and reinforces this theme.
The theme that Jesus' own people did not receive him is already present in the prologue: 'He came to what was his own, and his own people did not receive him' ([ref:Joh 1:11|John 1:11]).
Jesus is the only Son who is in the Father's bosom and has made God known ([ref:Joh 1:18|John 1:18]). He testifies to what he has seen with the Father.

Jesus says that he speaks what he has heard from the Father: 'The one who sent me is true, and I speak to the world what I have heard from him' ([ref:Joh 8:26|John 8:26]). This corresponds to his testifying about what he has seen and heard.
Jesus says: 'I speak of what I have seen with my Father' ([ref:Joh 8:38|John 8:38]). He testifies to what he has directly seen in the heavenly reality.

'Not that anyone has seen the Father except the one who is from God; he has seen the Father' ([ref:Joh 6:46|John 6:46]). Jesus is the only one who has seen the Father, and therefore his testimony is unique and authoritative.
Jesus says that his teaching is not his own but comes from him who sent him ([ref:Joh 7:16|John 7:16]). He testifies to what he has received directly from the Father.
The Son does only what he sees the Father doing ([ref:Joh 5:19-20|John 5:19-20]). Jesus' testimony is rooted in his unique relationship with the Father – he has seen and heard everything from him.

Despite the fact that Jesus had performed many signs, they did not believe in him. The quote from Isaiah emphasizes the people's unbelief ([ref:Joh 12:37-38|John 12:37-38]), which corresponds to 'no one accepts his testimony'.
Isaiah asks: 'Who has believed what we have heard?' ([ref:Jes 53:1|Isaiah 53:1]). This prophetic word predicted that the testimony of the Lord's servant would be rejected by many.

The next verse nuances the statement 'no one accepts' by saying that whoever accepts his testimony has confirmed that God is true ([ref:Joh 3:33|John 3:33]). 'No one' is thus used hyperbolically – very few accept it.
